tasks.short: Develop and maintain the project work breakdown structure.

steps.what: Collect approved scope, requirements, constraints and previous project templates.
Break deliverables into work packages and identify missing scope.

loop.input: Approved scope pack and work package template.
loop.output: Provisional work packages, source references and unresolved scope questions.
loop.check: Validate hierarchy, unique identifiers and source references; project manager checks scope coverage.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; unresolved items become scope questions for technical leads.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cannot reliably decompose novel requirements written in free text.

steps.what: Agree work package boundaries, estimates and dependencies with technical leads.
Enter the hierarchy, estimates and dependencies into the project plan.
Approve the baseline and associated scope, schedule and cost commitments.
Assess requested changes and propose revisions for the next baseline decision.
Copy the approved hierarchy into a parallel reporting workbook.

tasks.design: A reusable importer gathers approved material from {DOCS} and {PROJECT}; a bounded drafting loop proposes work packages with source references and open questions. Configured hierarchy checks and baseline controls in {PROJECT} support technical review and sponsor approval, while shared views replace the parallel {SPREADSHEET}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements varied, project templates were inconsistent, and transferring agreed detail into the plan took effort.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building importers and validators. Bounded drafting can propose an initial decomposition, with no assumed breakthrough in estimation.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden dependencies, architecture choices and incomplete scope still require technical discussion. Connectors and custom project fields can dominate implementation effort.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising omitted work and deciding which boundaries make delivery manageable.

ambition.what: Weekly scope-cut scenario review before milestones become threatened.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling and copying plans toward testing scope options with technical leads. Formal baseline approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Map interface dependencies into work package acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Interface contracts, dependency mapping and testable acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: Hierarchy validation, version controls and source imports can use deterministic technology.
GitHub Copilot supports coding and review assistance with expected human oversight.
An early developer trial found slower completion with AI; faster implementation is not guaranteed.

assumptions: This represents a project manager coordinating technical leads and a project sponsor.
The parallel workbook duplicates hierarchy data; unique reporting requirements would need migration.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Build ranges cover one reusable workflow and an initial project pilot; consultation waiting periods can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which project fields, exports and APIs are available?
Who approves baselines and which changes require renewed approval?
Does the reporting workbook contain unique calculations?
Can project documents be processed within the approved data boundary?
research_questions: Does a source-linked draft reduce total planning time after technical review?
Which hierarchy and dependency checks catch consequential omissions?
new_work: Review generated scope coverage and unresolved questions.
Maintain templates, field mappings and hierarchy checks.
Handle inaccessible sources and failed imports.
Check that baseline views retain the required audit history.

tasks.short: Review project team contributions, discuss feedback and document agreed support.

steps.what: Review agreed deliverables, progress, blockers and previous commitments.
Ask the team member about context, dependencies and support needs.
Form balanced feedback and decide which support or escalation is appropriate.
Discuss feedback, hear disagreement and agree practical next steps.
Write the feedback record and action dates in the restricted personnel record.
Send reminders about agreed actions and the next discussion.

tasks.design: Configure a restricted factual view in {PROJECT} showing agreed deliverables, blockers and commitments. A structured form in {TALENT}, or restricted {DOCS} where needed, captures human-written feedback and drives agreed reminders through {WORKFLOW}; it produces no individual scores or inferred assessments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery facts and private feedback notes lived in separate places. Automating assessment would also miss context and risk damaging trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing record permissions, configurable forms and scheduled reminders handle much of the preparation and follow-up. Small integrations can connect approved facts without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Attributing outcomes fairly and discussing difficult feedback remain human work. GDPR applies; national rules may require employee consultation, and an employee-evaluation extension would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Understanding circumstances, listening to disagreement and giving feedback that changes behaviour without undermining trust.

ambition.what: Fortnightly support-intervention review for blocked team members.

tasks.altitude: More time goes into coaching and removing blockers, with less preparation and reminder chasing. Formal appraisal and employment decision rights remain with the existing authorised roles.

reach.task: Investigate recurring process blockers across project teams.
reach.learn: Process mapping, contextual comparison and separating system constraints from individual contribution.

evidence.claim: Configured factual views, restricted records and reminders can reduce preparation without automating performance judgement.
Project activity measures alone do not establish an individual's performance or explain delivery problems.
The digest identifies Dutch works council consent provisions relevant to employee-monitoring systems.

assumptions: The project manager gives project feedback; the line manager retains formal appraisal responsibility.
The factual view uses declared project records rather than message analysis or passive activity tracking.
The employee can discuss and correct the factual basis of feedback.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Consent and access ranges include consultation preparation and access design; formal processes may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which feedback records may the project manager access and retain?
What national consultation requirements apply to the proposed factual view?
Does an existing {TALENT} form meet the team's needs?
Which delivery facts are reliable enough to show without misleading context?
research_questions: Does the factual view improve preparation without encouraging simplistic comparisons?
Which record fields help follow-through while minimising personal data?
new_work: Correct inaccurate delivery facts before feedback discussions.
Maintain access permissions and retention settings.
Review whether the view is drifting into employee scoring.

tasks.short: Coordinate project staffing needs, interviews and personnel selection.

steps.what: Check work packages, required dates and available internal capacity.
Specify responsibilities, essential skills, allocation, dates and cost limits.
Approve the staffing budget and internal or external sourcing route.
Compile authorised candidate profiles and existing application information for review.
Arrange interviews with candidates and the technical interview panel.
Interview candidates, discuss technical evidence and recommend a selection.
Approve the selected person and authorised appointment or allocation terms.
Record the authorised selection and pass allocation details to project planning.
Send candidates the approved selection outcome and next steps.

tasks.design: A staffing form links approved work packages in {PROJECT} to authorised capacity data from {HCM} and a requisition in {ATS}. Configured scheduling uses {CALENDAR}, while deterministic integrations carry approved decisions back to the staffing plan; candidate outcomes require recruiter approval before sending.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project demand, available capacity and recruitment records used different identifiers and approval routes. Email carried the coordination between them.
tasks.enabler_now: Configurable requisitions, scheduling and small field-mapping integrations can connect the process. No model is needed for the proposed coordination workflow.
tasks.still_hard: People still judge technical suitability, secure internal release and negotiate terms. GDPR and national employment rules apply; introducing automated candidate evaluation would require EU AI Act assessment.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining the real project need, evaluating technical evidence and negotiating a workable staffing commitment.

ambition.what: Project staffing scenario clinic comparing internal allocation, recruitment and scope reduction.

tasks.altitude: The project manager spends less time chasing availability and more time testing staffing alternatives with resource owners. Selection, budget and employment decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Build cross-project staffing scenarios before approving recruitment demand.
reach.learn: Capacity modelling, cost assumptions and resource-release constraints.

evidence.claim: Structured staffing requests, calendar scheduling and approved-decision synchronisation can use configured workflows and deterministic integrations.
AI systems used for recruitment or selection can fall within employment-related high-risk categories.
The digest provides no measured case establishing savings for project staffing coordination.

assumptions: Recruiters provide an authorised candidate pool; the integration neither discovers candidates nor ranks them.
Interview recipients and panel membership are set by a person before standard scheduling messages are sent.
The steps describe the recruitment route; internal allocation uses the corresponding resource-owner approval.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one staffing workflow.
Consent and access work includes candidate-data permissions and consultation assessment under national rules; waiting periods may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Are internal capacity and candidate records available through approved interfaces?
Who can authorise internal release, recruitment spend and appointment terms?
Which candidate communications must receive individual approval?
What candidate-data retention and sharing restrictions apply?
research_questions: Can capacity gaps be calculated without interpreting unstructured skill profiles?
Which scheduling exceptions still require recruiter intervention?
new_work: Maintain role, capacity and requisition field mappings.
Resolve conflicting availability and internal-release exceptions.
Review candidate outcome messages before sending.
Audit candidate-data access and remove expired temporary copies.

tasks.short: Allocate project work, clarify responsibilities and establish delegated authority.

steps.what: Review work packages, confirmed staffing, availability and existing authority limits.
Draft work assignments and a responsibility matrix.
Agree ownership, handoffs, workload trade-offs and escalation responsibilities.
Approve decision rights, spending limits and escalation thresholds.
Record approved owners, responsibilities and authority references against work packages.
Circulate assignments and tell affected colleagues where decisions and escalations belong.

tasks.design: A deterministic generator combines approved work packages in {PROJECT}, declared capacity from {HCM} and responsibility templates from {DOCS} to propose allocations and flag conflicts. After team agreement and sponsor approval of authority, an integration updates {PROJECT} and configured notifications distribute the approved assignments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Capacity, work packages and delegation policies were maintained separately. Responsibility matrices also became stale after manual copying.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit capacity constraints and reusable role templates support deterministic proposals. AI-assisted coding can make the field mappings and validation checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Declared capacity can conceal competing commitments. Negotiating ownership and delegating consequential decisions require trust, context and authorised approval.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who can accept a responsibility and resolving conflicts between delivery needs, development opportunities and existing commitments.
tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving ownership gaps and negotiating capacity before work stalls. Existing delegation limits determine which reallocations the project manager may approve.

reach.task: Coordinate shared administrative support across competing project milestones.
reach.learn: Service capacity planning, priority negotiation and explicit handoff agreements.

evidence.claim: Explicit capacity and role constraints can generate allocation proposals and identify missing or conflicting ownership deterministically.
Human negotiation remains necessary where several feasible allocations have different organisational consequences.
GitHub Copilot provides coding assistance that can support implementation, with oversight.

assumptions: Capacity and eligible roles are explicitly declared; no employee ability or performance is inferred.
Proposals remain provisional until team agreement and the required authority approval.
Recording delegated authority does not itself grant technical access permissions.
GDPR applies to staffing data; national rules determine any employee consultation required.
Time shares and build ranges estimate a pilot using one responsibility template; consultation waiting periods may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Are capacity records current across projects?
Which role constraints and delegation limits can be expressed explicitly?
Who approves routine reallocations and changes to authority?
Which consultations and data-access permissions are required?
research_questions: Do deterministic proposals reduce negotiation time after capacity conflicts are exposed?
Which constraints should block publication rather than display a warning?
new_work: Maintain capacity inputs and responsibility templates.
Resolve infeasible allocations and conflicting project priorities.
Check published assignments against approved delegation decisions.
Retire outdated responsibilities when scope or staffing changes.

role.altitude: The project manager spends less time assembling records and coordinating routine handoffs, and more time shaping scope, negotiating capacity and coaching delivery. Sponsors, hiring managers and line managers retain their existing approval rights.
reach: Computer systems analysis: connect work package boundaries to interface dependencies and acceptance criteria.
Management analysis: investigate recurring delivery constraints across teams.
Project management specialisation: compare staffing and scope scenarios across projects.
Administrative services management: negotiate shared support capacity around project milestones.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a lightweight project-options service that brings scope, capacity and delivery evidence into recurring sponsor decisions, while keeping personnel judgement and consequential commitments with authorised people.
